context: Drop the positional capability argument and run argv exactly as the operator wrote it, leaving TODO_DB_CREDENTIAL_CAPABILITY in the child environment as the sole capability channel; a wrapper script that needs conditional logic reads it, and plain retrieval commands then work verbatim. Capture bytes instead of text: enforce CREDENTIAL_COMMAND_MAX_BYTES against the raw bytes first, then decode with errors='replace', so no decode path can raise. Update ADR 0005 G4 to describe the environment-only capability channel and to note that the memoization key covers argv, the capability, and the configured command string but not the whole child environment. Update the README paragraph and the runbook. Add regression tests that run a real argument-strict provider stub which fails if given an unexpected positional, and a provider returning invalid UTF-8.
description: Adversarial review of PR #18 by Antigravity (agy 1.1.14, gemini-3.1-pro-high, effort high) returned one Blocker and one Required finding, both verified against the real tools. BLOCKER: _provider_credential runs [*argv, capability], so the exact command documented in README.md and the runbook executes as `security find-generic-password -w -s todo-db-rw read-write`; security's grammar is `[-s service] [options...] [keychain...]`, so the trailing word becomes the keychain to search and the command exits 44. A non-zero exit is an error by design, so the operator gets E_AUTH_MISSING and the feature fails on first use by following its own documentation. `op read` and `pass show` fail the same way. REQUIRED: subprocess.run(..., text=True) decodes strictly inside communicate(), so non-UTF-8 provider output raises UnicodeDecodeError, which is a ValueError and slips past every except clause, crashing the process and bypassing the E_AUTH_MISSING degradation ADR 0005 G4 mandates. The finding that the provider cache should be keyed by database is rebutted: the provider is never told which database it is asked about, so the cache key already covers every input it receives; record that as a documented limitation instead.

anti_patterns.dont: Catch UnicodeDecodeError around subprocess.run and call it fixed
anti_patterns.instead: capture bytes so no decode can raise at all
anti_patterns.why: strict decoding inside communicate can still mangle or discard output paths

anti_patterns.dont: Decode provider output before enforcing the size bound
anti_patterns.instead: bound the raw bytes first, then decode with replacement
anti_patterns.why: a huge or malformed payload would then be decoded in full before being rejected

anti_patterns.dont: Keep the positional capability and tell operators to wrap every provider in a script
anti_patterns.instead: pass the capability through the child environment only
anti_patterns.why: the documented one-line examples are the whole usability argument for this feature and a mandatory wrapper reintroduces setup burden

anti_patterns.dont: Write provider test stubs that accept any arguments
anti_patterns.instead: include a stub that exits non-zero on an unexpected positional
anti_patterns.why: that is exactly why the review found this defect and the test suite did not

preserves.behavior: A non-zero exit, timeout, missing executable, unparsable command, or oversized output remains an error that stops resolution and never reads as an absent credential.
Only exit 0 with empty output permits read-only to fall back to read-write.
Provider stdout and stderr never reach an exception, log, doctor field, or tracker evidence; failures still report argv[0] and the exit status only.
The output size limit is still enforced, now against raw bytes before any decode can run.
The provider still never runs through a shell: argv comes from shlex.split and subprocess.run is called with shell=False.
With TODO_DB_CREDENTIAL_COMMAND unset, resolution outcomes, codes, capability selection, and exit statuses are unchanged.
